feedback: The reward machine is semantically faithful, well-formed, and format-compliant. Task reading: success requires target_picked_up (which entails door_open occurred, since the box room has no other entrance), while the episode must never contain both key_lost and door_open; since the goal forces door_open, the constraint reduces to never firing key_lost, and the RM encodes exactly this successful set. Verification: (1) Ordered progress chain u0->u1 (blocker_moved), u1->u2 (has_door_key & blocker_moved), u2->u3 (door_open), u3->u6 (target_picked_up) matches the only viable order — ball first, then key, then door, then box; the key-first route is correctly doomed because dropping the key while the door is closed fires key_lost, and the u0/u1/u2 key_lost edges divert to u4, from which any later door_open completes the violation (u4->u5, -1.0) and u6 is unreachable. (2) The reverse order is covered: in u3 (door already opened), a later key_lost (door toggled shut, key dropped) routes to u5 with -1.0, so both event orders of the forbidden conjunction are punished exactly once. (3) Guards are satisfiable and never block a viable path: at the ball pickup has_door_key is false (ball in hand); at the key pickup blocker_moved is true unless the ball was returned to the door cell, which is a genuinely doomed situation the RM correctly refuses to advance; at the toggle step blocker_moved, has_door_key, and !key_lost all necessarily hold; key_lost cannot co-occur with door_open, has_door_key, or target_picked_up per the environment constraints. (4) Non-latching conditions are handled correctly: blocker_moved and door_open regressions are absorbed by else self-loops without state corruption, and crucially the u1/u2/u3 else-loops prevent re-earning progress rewards when a condition flickers back (no unbounded reward farming). (5) key_lost is correctly used as a one-step event label; conditions are used only as step guards. (6) Every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant events (turns, moves, done, no-op pickups/drops). (7) Rewards are dense on the viable path (0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0), bounded, given once per milestone, with a single -1.0 per completed violation; failed-but-unpunished endings (key_lost with the door never opened) correctly yield no success since u6 stays unreachable, matching the task's successful set exactly. (8) FINAL_STATES header is present and nonempty (u6), u6 is declared in STATES and is the accepting state reached precisely on target_picked_up. (9) All states are reachable, the automaton is compact (u4/u5 split is justified to avoid double punishment), labels are predicate-only, the reward entries match the transition guards exactly, and the header/section layout follows the paper format.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are defined exactly once, with no extra functions, no imports, no actions, and no side effects; the code is syntactically valid. `blocker_moved` scans for the (unique) door and checks the cell to its left, which is equivalent to the canonical check of the cell at (dx-1, dy): it is true while the ball is carried (off-grid) and false again if the ball is dropped back on that cell, since only the current grid state is read. `has_door_key`, `door_open`, and `target_picked_up` match the canonical expressions exactly, including the color-matched door scan for the key, the is_open reading, and the mission-string match for the designated box. `key_lost` correctly implements the event semantics: it reads `env.episode_memory['previous_valuation']` in a read-only manner, requires prev `has_door_key` true, and recomputes the current `has_door_key` and `door_open` expressions inline (equivalent to `prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D`), so it fires for exactly the one step on which the key is dropped while the door is closed, is false on the first step (prev has_door_key false), and can never co-occur with `has_door_key`, `door_open`, or `target_picked_up`. The predicates only read env state (grid.get, carrying, mission, episode_memory) and never mutate the environment or episode memory.
